You have governed international HR vendors and can balance service quality, compliance, commercial terms, and cost control across stakeholders. Bonus Experience in digital assets, fintech, or another regulated industry. Familiarity with EOR/PEO employment models or entity-establishment projects. Experience with multi-currency, multi-jurisdiction payroll platforms or providers such as ADP, Deel, or TMF.

review_candidates.title: Executive Assistant to the Chairman
review_candidates.description: Executive Assistant to the Chairman Location: Gibraltar Full-time role About the company Based in Gibraltar, Fairhomes is an established international business group with interests spanning real estate development and a diverse range of other ventures. Led by an entrepreneurial Chairman, the group combines commercial ambition with a practical approach to bringing new ideas to life. Supporting the Chairman means working across varied businesses, projects and personal commitments. No two days are the same. This role will suit someone who enjoys variety, adapts quickly and brings structure and organisation to a busy entrepreneurial environment. The opportunity We are seeking a highly capable, organised and down-to-earth Executive Assistant to support the Chairman across a varied range of business and personal matters. You will need to understand business priorities, work accurately with figures, prepare clear information and see tasks through to completion. Just as important is your approach: practical, considerate and willing to help, whether you are coordinating a business project or sorting out an everyday arrangement. Working closely with the Chairman, colleagues and external advisers, you will keep information and actions organised, ask questions when something is unclear and use sound judgement about what needs attention. The role also includes personal, travel and property administration, requiring the same ownership, accuracy and discretion. Occasional support outside normal working hours, including late evenings and weekends, may be required. Discretion and confidentiality are paramount, and the successful candidate must exercise absolute integrity when handling sensitive business, financial, personal and family matters. Fluency in both Spanish and English, spoken and written, is essential, alongside strong Excel skills, numeracy and excellent IT capability. Key responsibilities Business support and project coordination Prepare concise briefings, research and summaries to help the Chairman assess opportunities, issues and priorities. Analyse and summarise financial and operational information in Excel, identifying discrepancies, trends and questions requiring attention. Attend meetings as required, capture decisions and coordinate follow-up actions with senior colleagues and external advisers. Track progress across business projects and commitments, highlighting delays, dependencies and matters requiring a decision. Review incoming information and correspondence, bringing clarity to complex matters and ensuring the Chairman is well prepared. Diary and communication Manage the Chairman’s business and personal diary, coordinating meetings, appointments, calls, social engagements and events. Handle changing priorities and last-minute requests, ensuring arrangements remain coordinated and all relevant details are available. Manage correspondence, prepare briefings and meeting materials, and maintain reminders and follow-up actions. Liaise professionally with colleagues, business contacts, advisers and service providers on the Chairman’s behalf. Communicate confidently in English and Spanish, including translating correspondence and documents when required. Travel and events Organise business, personal and family travel, including flights, accommodation, transfers, cars and drivers. Research and compare options, balancing convenience, cost and individual preferences. Prepare detailed itineraries and coordinate conference registrations, event attendance and restaurant reservations. Maintain accurate travel-day records and supporting information for tax and residency purposes, providing summaries to professional advisers as required. Personal and family support Coordinate personal and family administration, recurring commitments and important dates. Research and arrange gifts, purchases, deliveries and other personal requests. Handle private and family matters sensitively and with complete discretion. Property and household coordination Coordinate bookings and day-to-day arrangements for company apartments, ensuring they are maintained and prepared for visiting colleagues and guests. Arrange cleaning, repairs, supplies, keys and access, following up on issues until resolved. Support the administration of private properties in the UK and overseas, liaising with property managers, contractors and suppliers. Financial and general administration Coordinate authorised payments, invoices and recurring financial commitments, maintaining accurate records. Liaise with banks, accountants, tax advisers and insurers, gathering documents and following up on queries. Track insurance renewals and vehicle administration, obtaining and comparing quotations where appropriate. Create and maintain Excel spreadsheets, reports and trackers, checking figures and identifying discrepancies. Maintain organised digital records and research and coordinate a wide variety of business and personal requests. Essential skills and experience Proven commercial experience supporting a senior business leader in a demanding environment, or a strong background in business operations, finance or project coordination. Good business understanding and numerical ability, with the ability to interpret financial information and prepare clear, accurate summaries. Fluent English and Spanish: excellent spoken and written communication in both languages, with the ability to correspond independently and translate routine correspondence accurately. Exceptional organisational skills: able to manage multiple workstreams, changing priorities and detailed arrangements without losing sight of outstanding tasks. Strong Excel skills: confident using widely used formulas and spreadsheet functions to organise, analyse and present information accurately. Strong numeracy: comfortable checking figures, comparing costs and working with financial information. Excellent IT skills: confident using Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, online booking platforms and digital filing systems, with the ability to learn new tools quickly. Discretion and confidentiality are paramount: a proven ability to handle sensitive business, financial, personal and family information with absolute integrity. Sound judgement and initiative, including knowing when to act independently and when to seek guidance or approval. A practical, cost-conscious approach and the persistence to resolve issues and follow tasks through. A personable, down-to-earth approach and a good sense of humour, balanced with professionalism and discretion. About you You combine strong business and organisational skills with a friendly, grounded manner. You listen carefully, take pride in doing things well and treat everyone with courtesy and respect, whatever their role. You are comfortable working independently and taking initiative, while being equally willing to ask for guidance, welcome feedback and learn from others. You bring the same care to everyday administration as you do to more complex business matters. You enjoy solving problems, helping others and making a busy working day run smoothly. A good sense of humour will help you feel at home with a Chairman who values warmth, approachability and a down-to-earth working style. How to apply Please submit your CV and a short covering letter outlining your relevant experience, your proficiency in English and Spanish, and examples of work or personal achievements that demonstrate your suitability for the role. Applicants must be fluent in both English and Spanish. Language proficiency and Excel ability will be assessed during the recruitment process.
